name: Restored Media, Tracks & Ghost Suppression
purpose: Serve and analyse the restored original recordings and dataset splits without a camera: read-only catalog, calibrated detection overlay, metric ground tracks, playback flow and the ghost-suppression rule that guarantees two served frames never describe one object twice.

public_interfaces.name: read-only media catalog (media_roots / source_index_for_output)
public_interfaces.contract: Catalogues restored videos and dataset splits with stable ids and checksums; never mutates the underlying files.

public_interfaces.name: calibrated detection cache (detect_for_media)
public_interfaces.contract: Person/machinery boxes on native frames with a bounded cache and explicit disabled state when weights are absent.

public_interfaces.name: metric ground tracks + ground plane fit
public_interfaces.contract: Metric tracks, zone membership and a fitted ground plane per media source, shaped for the digital-twin packet.

public_interfaces.name: ghost suppression contract
public_interfaces.contract: At most one served detection per real object per frame; operator rows are kept visible.

acceptance_criteria: The catalog lists every restored video and dataset split without a camera present.
Ghost suppression holds under the randomised invariant test and at threshold boundaries.
A ground plane fitted from a recording yields metric tracks consistent with the calibrated band.
Playback stays smooth at the documented presentation format (1080p / 30 fps).
risks: Recorded media is demo evidence only; treating restored clips as site validation is explicitly forbidden by the validation policy.
The catalog depends on Git LFS media that may be absent in a shallow clone; absent assets must degrade to an explicit unavailable state.
